answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybils with escalating action fees: every identity pays a tiny copper-priced fee for each transaction, and the price rises steeply when one identity bursts many actions at once. A single honest agent trading at a normal pace barely notices the cost, like taking one walnut from a large orchard. A Sybil farmer spawning thousands of clones, however, must pay the escalating fee for every clone, so flooding the market costs far more than any gain. Fees can be recycled into an oasis fund rewarding verified honest participants, turning attack cost into public benefit.
